name: Boston
publicWasteDetail: Analyze Boston provides 311 Service Requests and a daily Moving Truck Permits dataset.
mattressCollectionType: Curbside by appointment for most buildings with 6 units or fewer
knownMattressPartner: Private haulers; city mattress pickup program
reportingGapSummary: Boston has strong public operational data, but no citywide public item-level furniture reporting system for reusable furniture left curbside.
suggestedAction: Create a cross-neighborhood furniture reporting layer that links curb alerts, pickup requests, and reuse outlets.
tooltipSummary: Strong public waste data exists, but reusable furniture is still poorly tracked as a distinct stream.

name: Allston
publicWasteDetail: Boston neighborhood-level analysis can be built from 311 and Moving Truck Permits; Allston is explicitly identified as the Allston Christmas hotspot.
knownPartner: Household Goods / Boston coordinated furniture pilot
reportingGapSummary: Allston is central to the annual move-out surge, but furniture left curbside is not publicly counted in a reusable, item-level way.
suggestedAction: Prioritize Allston for real-time curb reports, condition tags, and pickup/donation matching.
tooltipSummary: The clearest hotspot for coordinated used-furniture reporting during September move-out.

name: Brighton
publicWasteDetail: Can be analyzed through Boston 311 and Moving Truck Permits as part of the September move corridor.
knownPartner: Household Goods / Boston coordinated furniture pilot
reportingGapSummary: Brighton shares the move-out pressure of Allston but lacks an item-level public used-furniture reporting layer.
suggestedAction: Bundle Brighton with Allston in the first phase of a reporting-and-pickup pilot.
tooltipSummary: A strong candidate for the same used-furniture reporting system as Allston.

name: Cambridge
publicWasteDetail: Cambridge now publishes daily, monthly, and yearly waste datasets; monthly data includes mattresses and box springs, and yearly data includes weekly trash per household.
mattressCollectionType: Free weekly curbside pickup by appointment
reportingGapSummary: Cambridge has the strongest public waste reporting structure in this project scope, but still lacks a public, item-level used-furniture availability/reporting feed.
suggestedAction: Use Cambridge as the model city for a furniture-reporting layer linked to existing waste and permit data.
tooltipSummary: Best municipal model for open waste reporting, but reusable furniture still needs its own public layer.

name: Somerville
publicWasteDetail: Statewide municipal survey data available through MassDEP; Recycle Smart lists Somerville mattress collection as curbside.
reportingGapSummary: Somerville has a mattress program but no obvious public, item-level furniture reporting feed in the source set.
suggestedAction: Add Somerville as a regional partner node in a shared map and reporting standard.
tooltipSummary: Has curbside mattress collection, but furniture reporting is still missing.

name: Watertown
publicWasteDetail: Statewide municipal survey data available through MassDEP; Recycle Smart lists Watertown mattress collection as curbside.
reportingGapSummary: Watertown could be folded into a regional reporting map because residents face disposal choices but little public used-furniture visibility.
suggestedAction: Add a simple curbside reporting intake and donation-routing layer.
tooltipSummary: Good fit for a regional used-furniture map connected to Boston and Cambridge.

name: Arlington
publicWasteDetail: Statewide municipal survey data available through MassDEP; Recycle Smart lists Arlington mattress collection as curbside.
reportingGapSummary: A likely regional participant in a standardized furniture-reporting system.
suggestedAction: Support shared standards for item condition, pickup windows, and donation routing.
tooltipSummary: Has mattress collection but lacks public used-furniture reporting.

name: Belmont
publicWasteDetail: Statewide municipal survey data available through MassDEP; Recycle Smart lists Belmont mattress collection as curbside.
reportingGapSummary: Belmont residents likely have reuse opportunities, but not through a shared public reporting interface.
suggestedAction: Use the regional map to connect Belmont households to nearby reuse channels.
tooltipSummary: A good example of a city with mattress service but no furniture reporting layer.

name: Chelsea
publicWasteDetail: Statewide municipal survey data available through MassDEP; Recycle Smart lists Chelsea mattress collection as drop-off and curbside.
reportingGapSummary: Chelsea already uses a mixed access model for mattresses, which could be mirrored in a furniture-reporting and pickup system.
suggestedAction: Test mixed reporting flows for both curbside and drop-off users.
tooltipSummary: A mixed collection model city that would benefit from coordinated furniture reporting.

name: Newton
publicWasteDetail: Statewide municipal survey data available through MassDEP; Recycle Smart lists Newton mattress collection as drop-off and curbside.
reportingGapSummary: Newton fits a regional system that supports both curbside and drop-off pathways but still needs public furniture visibility.
suggestedAction: Standardize condition labels and pickup availability with neighboring municipalities.
tooltipSummary: Has multiple mattress pathways, but furniture is still invisible in public reporting.

name: Malden
publicWasteDetail: Statewide municipal survey data available through MassDEP; Recycle Smart lists Malden mattress collection as curbside.
reportingGapSummary: Malden would benefit from a simple regional furniture reporting protocol tied to mattress collection information.
suggestedAction: Include Malden in the first ring of metro-area data standardization.
tooltipSummary: Curbside mattress access exists, but reusable furniture is not publicly tracked.

name: Revere
publicWasteDetail: Statewide municipal survey data available through MassDEP; Recycle Smart lists Revere mattress collection as curbside.
reportingGapSummary: Revere illustrates how many cities have mattress access information but no public used-furniture reporting layer.
suggestedAction: Add Revere to a metro-area furniture availability and pickup reporting map.
tooltipSummary: Public mattress access is clearer than public furniture-reuse visibility.

name: UTEC Mattress Recycling
publicWasteDetail: Listed by Bye Bye Mattress as a Massachusetts mattress recycler; Cambridge identifies UTEC as its mattress recycling partner.
reportingGapSummary: Important backend infrastructure exists, but the public lacks a coordinated front-end map for reusable furniture before items become waste.
suggestedAction: Show backend recyclers on the same map as curb alerts and donation options.
tooltipSummary: A critical recycler that should appear on the same public map as used-furniture reporting.

name: Conigliaro Industries
publicWasteDetail: Listed by Bye Bye Mattress as a Massachusetts mattress recycler; Recycle Smart lists Framingham mattress collection as drop-off and curbside.
reportingGapSummary: Framingham demonstrates that processing infrastructure exists, but is not yet tied to a public-facing used-furniture reporting network.
suggestedAction: Use recycler nodes as destinations in the same map as donation and curbside reporting.
tooltipSummary: Processing exists; public coordination is what is missing.

name: Green Mattress Co. - North Andover
publicWasteDetail: Listed by Bye Bye Mattress and on Green Mattress Co. website.
reportingGapSummary: Backend recyclers are visible to insiders, but not integrated into a public used-furniture decision map.

name: Tough Stuff Recycling Facility
publicWasteDetail: Listed by Bye Bye Mattress as a Massachusetts recycler.

tooltipSummary: A backend recycling destination that can anchor the map’s infrastructure layer.
